    <p style="text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; font-size: 0.85rem; color: #555; margin-top: 0.25rem;">
    Graduate Research Assistant
    </p>
    <p>Malory Wissing is a third-year Ph.D. student in Industrial-Organizational Psychology at Colorado State University. She earned her Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Auburn University in 2019. Through her research, Malory explores how work as a calling extends beyond the workplace to impact employees' broader lives and relationships. Specifically, her developing research focuses on the prosocial aspects of calling and "nonwork" outcomes, understanding how meaningful work influences family life, community engagement, and overall well-being. Currently, she is conducting a systematic review of calling and the work-family interface and exploring the role of time in work-nonwork balance. She is also interested in how individuals' understanding of their calling may shape their relationship with work and spousal relationship quality.</p>
